response:
**I found one concrete semantic defect in the implemented typed-defense path.** The save-half → flat → resistance correction itself is consistent with the governing decision.

Operative **Petrified does not supply poison-damage immunity to a character without innate poison immunity**:

- [SharedTypedDamage.cs](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/9cbac60eefbe8f61b11b5e2adebde8b194961aad/engine/com.decennium.foundation/Laboratory/Model/SharedTypedDamage.cs#L15) obtains immunity only from `CreatureActorRecord.DamageImmunities`.
- [TypedDamageRecords.cs](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/9cbac60eefbe8f61b11b5e2adebde8b194961aad/engine/com.decennium.foundation/Runtime/Core/TypedDamageRecords.cs#L23) uses Petrified only for resistance halving.
- Consequently, a Petrified character receiving poison4, with no flat reduction or innate immunity, resolves to **2 rather than0**. This is a source-level counterexample; I did not execute it in C#.
- The pinned [Petrified procedure](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/46a4d52728ee6956f0bebcb5d2103ffd5bc67ba4/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md#petrified) grants poison immunity. Existing prevention of the **Poisoned condition** does not implement poison-damage immunity.

The current controls mask this omission: the ordinary-character Petrified cases use fire, while the poison cases use the already poison-immune Wraith.

Correct this within TAC-10’s typed path, retaining event-time condition provenance. The record validator currently assumes immunity provenance is exclusively innate, so it also needs the corresponding distinction. Ending Petrified later must not invalidate legitimate historical protection; fabricated protection must still fail causal validation.

Add labeled shared-pipeline controls for a character without innate immunity covering operative, wholly suppressed and ended Petrified, independent immunity overlap, and actual HP/tempHP/RNG consequences. Suppressing only Petrified’s inherited Incapacitated component must not remove its remaining protection. Preserve historical95–113 behavior and encoding.

I found no additional concrete defect in the reviewed numeric conversion and newly routed consumers:

- Creature untrained contribution remains0 while PB remains unavailable.
- Target ability facts are separated from the real source owner’s class/PB.
- Suppression Fire passes raw damage plus its save result, avoiding a second save half.
- The corrected record stages agree with the resolver.
- Hunting-trap typed routing remains explicitly versioned.

My independent reconciliation covered:

- The exact evidence commit `d9c67114b0a96bf6369d71c696a441ede6f11bee`, with an empty engine diff from frozen `9cbac60e`.
- Archive hash/length and **all89 members**, totaling9,904,757 expanded bytes.
- **465 compilation-input hashes**, **971 static-input hashes**, four retained DLL hashes and linked reports.
- All22 individual passing records against their aggregate, seven retained genesis checks, five identical genesis saves, executed driver/host bindings and the failed collector’s zero cases.
- Independent arithmetic checks of all32 ordered-damage rows.

I did **not** compile, execute the binaries, restore saves or rerun those cases. Separate read-only reviews covered damage and numeric-target changes. The reports substantiate partial coverage; they do not establish every converted producer’s creature-target behavior.

This correction requires no new prerequisite module. Independent admission/seal/controller work can continue within TAC-10. Genuine creature execution, complete consumer reconciliation, five paths, compatibility, full regression and actual final review remain mandatory; no module acceptance or successor authorization is given.
